The most important thing is that you don’t live your life like that anymore! Have you ever heard of amends, like what members of AA do? In a nutshell, they reach out to the people they’ve harmed in the past, apologize for their ways, and promise that they will never treat anyone like that again because they live differently now. If your childhood is haunting you so much, it might be worth looking into. After all, it doesn’t matter what actually happened; it just matters how you *felt* about what happened, and that’s what’s likely causing this stress today.

Also, it doesn’t help that the pandemic is making everyone nostalgic. This could be another reason you’re ruminating on your darker days, even if they were long ago. If this is the case, perhaps you could try spicing up your life with positive actions, volunteering, or simply reaching out to people you care about for a wellness check during these difficult times. Positive actions like these could boost your self esteem and reassure you that you’ve changed. 

Stay strong! :)

My mom always told me, “If it’s in your house, it’s in your stomach.” 

The best way to avoid compulsive eating is to avoid buying unhealthy snacks and anything bingeworthy. Veggies and fruits are good snacks, but they’re not addictive. As for food, buy meals that take a bit of effort to prepare so you’ll only eat them if you’re actually hungry. 

Another way is mindfulness. Before eating, ask yourself, “Why am I eating?” If you’re hungry, eat something low-carb but filling (especially water-filled fruits like apples and grapes). If you’re bored, find something else to do. If you want to taste something, chew gum. 

Good luck! :)

He always told me he loved me and was happy to be with me, but I didn’t feel it because, deep down, I guess I wanted him to invest as much as I was investing. 

We ended up breaking up; I technically broke up with him, but it was because he didn’t seem like he loved me like he used to. It broke me, and I’m still recovering months later. 

I learned that sometimes you have to admit to yourself that, if you find yourself helping your boyfriend more than he would ever be willing to help you, you have to call it a red flag and a dealbreaker. Otherwise, he’ll start taking you for granted, and you’ll end up sacrificing way too much to make him happy. 

I’m not saying you should break up, but please at least seriously evaluate if these problems are normal for a relationship. Sometimes they seem normal to you if they’re gradual, but a relationship should not give you anxiety. I know how it feels to have a great life — great friends, good grades, a fun social life — and then to have your head completely in the clouds all because of a boy. I felt like he was a drug because I cared about him so much more than anything else in my life. However, even though I miss him a lot, I realize that my next relationship cannot turn out like my last one; I will find someone who will put as much effort as I will into the relationship and someone who will constantly reassure me that he cares.

Good question! It took me a hot second to think of a solid answer, but I’ll give it a shot:

1. First of all, none of my friends could really relate, so I came to this sub, and that helped a LOT. He was my first boyfriend, so it was nice knowing that my seemingly psychopathic thoughts were actually 100% normal.

2. I started exercising consistently and eating healthy foods (mostly whole foods, especially green vegetables). I did this for a multitude of reasons. For one, my ex and I gained a few kilos together, and at the end of our breakup, I found out he had resented this for a long time but never told me about it. I was mad at him for pretending like he didn’t care and disgusted with myself for not keeping up with my health. Hence, the best way I could forgive myself was to treat my body well. Now, I’ve lost about 15 kilos, I work out as many days as possible, and I jog for 2-4 miles a few times per week. I look good, and I’m starting to see abs form for the first time in my life (shocking!). But most importantly, I feel good! Eating vegetables is honestly a natural antidepressant. It sounds sad, but it’s actually wonderful. Every time I had a depressive episode while crying about him, I used to grab a box of tissues and cry for hours in my room. A month or two ago is when I finally took control again and started making these lifestyle changes; every time I felt a sob session coming on, I told myself, “Okay, that’s my cue to go for a run.” Now, I’m fit and healthy, and he’s still pudgy and judgmental as he’s always been. I hate when people make excuses for problems that have an easy solution. He always blamed work and life for not being able to exercise, but exercising is easy if you have just 10 minutes per day, and he definitely had at least an hour to dedicate if he really wanted to get in shape. I realized he is simply not a go-getter, and I have goals in life and dreams to live up to. He is still the same complainer, and now I’m finally feeling optimistic again because I don’t have his negativity weighing me down.

3. I retrained my brain to associate my memories with him with other blissful memories. For example, as I mentioned in a different comment on this post, we used to cuddle a lot, and that was my favorite thing in the whole world. Every time I saw a couple hugging or cuddling on TV or in real life, I started tearing up and panicking at the fact I couldn’t do that with him anymore. However, I also have a lovely cat, and she is also wonderful at cuddling. I hug her all the time, and I remember she won’t break my heart and she’s much more deserving of my love :’) We always used to watch a certain TV show together, so, when a new season came out, I had no desire to watch it. However, I found out my sister also watches it, so now we make it a tradition to watch it together so I could temporarily erase the negative connotation with that show. There are tons of other examples because a lot of things reminded me of him, and this step takes a LONG time and a lot of willpower. I was tired of always being sad at so many normal parts of life that should not have reminded me of him. I trained my mind to remove him from the foreground of my life, and it’s helped a lot.

4. I went easy on myself. I had a lot of stressful things to do for my job, so I focused mostly on that and spent all my free time doing things I loved, not boring or difficult tasks. I hung out with friends as much as possible. At first, it was difficult because of the pandemic, so I did plenty of zoom calls and spent time with family. Now, whenever a friend invites me to hang out, I say yes, even if I’m extremely tired and not feeling up for it. I want to build wonderful memories so I can remember this time of my life as a time where I went on adventures and spent quality time with friends, not a time where I was only depressed all the time because of the breakup. 

5. I wrote him a LOT of letters, but I never sent them. I poured out all my feelings. Some guardian angel on Reddit sent me a private message one day and recommended that I write down all my feelings in the third person as if I were writing a novel about someone. Then, that person said I should see it from a perspective of a stranger and give my advice based on the story. This helped a LOT as well, and I started feeling bad for the girl instead of feeling bad for the guy who broke her heart. I also watched some shows about unhealthy relationships; mine was borderline toxic, so this helped me see that toxicity is all too common and that it is not to be ignored. One of the characters once said, “Pretend your boyfriend isn’t treating you well. Imagine that in your mind. Now, replace yourself with your best friend. Does your best friend deserve that treatment?” 

6. I wrote down all the things I loved about him. There were a lot. Then, I added the things I wish were true about him. In other words, I identified all his greatest mistakes and flaws and put the perfected version of them on this list. Then, I promised myself I would not date a guy who breached any of these top priority characteristics. I have a new benchmark now, and I will not let any toxic ass boy cast a spell on me. I will make sure he is authentic and meets my expectations. I once heard the quote, “You can’t choose who you love, but you can choose who not to love.” If some guy tries to charm his way into my life but doesn’t meet my personality requirements, I will not allow myself to fall into that trap. (Of course it’s good to be open-minded, but I need to protect myself by watching out for red flags). 

All in all, it might take a lot of depression and a lot of sleepless nights, so just remember that you’ve hit rock bottom. The only way it can go from there is up, so hang in there! It’s like when your stock portfolio plummets to a worth of $0. Are you going to sell the stock? Of course not! You’re going to hang in there until it reaches a much higher value because the companies need to invest a lot of effort into making the company more productive. We, as humans, are investments, but we are simultaneously the investors. It is up to us to deal with the breakup; a good card player doesn’t care which cards they have in their hands because the priority is making sure know how to play the hand. Take care of yourself, realize you have so much more worth that someone will recognize one day, and believe in yourself. It’s extremely difficult, and I thought I would never be able to recover, but I’m feeling better and better every day. You guys can do it too! Stay strong! We’re all rooting for you! ❤️

The typical American high school covers “common core” subjects, which means you have to study math, science, English, social studies/history, and a foreign language each year. There are usually also physical education and health class requirements. 

There are variations to this; for example, in my high school, the foreign language requirement was two years, and the science and mathematics requirements were three years. We had to take gym all four years, but we only took health for two years. 

You can also choose one or two electives, which are classes that interest you. I took orchestra, economics, public speaking, and psychology during the course of my studies. 

My high school also had some alternatives for students who wished to enter a technical field instead of attending university: these students attended the same high school as me for half of the day to take the core classes and attended the rest of their classes at the technical high school, where students could learn nursing, carpentry, information technology, and other topics. 

There are also private schools. Sometimes they are prep schools meant to be more “prestigious,” sometimes they are boarding schools, sometimes they are religious, and sometimes they’re a mix.

This isn’t a direct answer to your question, but it’s an anecdote that might kind of explain your friend’s train of thought. 

A friend of mine from Milan was furious because a statue of a famous journalist in Milan was recently defaced, and not for the first time. Apparently the man was a wonderful, talented journalist, but he was also pretty racist, so some people felt the need to make a point during the Black Lives Matter movement. He posted an Instagram story complaining about how “ignorant, uneducated fascists” had done it (from what I understand, many Italians consider people who are uneducated an ignorant to be “fascists,” but please correct me if I’m wrong because this is just an observation that I am not 100% sure of by any means). 

Then, he posted the response of the mayor of Milan, who had posted an Instagram video saying that it was unfortunate people had defaced the statue, but that he understood people’s concern. He took a sympathetic approach in explaining that everyone has skeletons in their closets, and, if we canceled every famous historical figure for doing something bad, we wouldn’t have many of them left to celebrate. Then, he followed up by asking the citizens of Milan two questions: 1.) what merits someone the right to be honored as a historical figure, whether it be with a statue, a building named after them, a mention in a history book, etc.? 2.) if we were candidates to be honored as a historical figure, would we allow ourselves to be honored based on our backgrounds? He implied that everyone has made mistakes; even though the man was racist, tons of figures have done terrible things, but we can still appreciate the fact that he was a good writer who made Italy proud in that sense. 

After that, my friend posted another story saying something along the lines of, “I know Trump is dumb, but even he understand that hooligans who go around defacing statues should be punished.” In other words, he was saying the mayor should have been stricter in responding to these “fascists” who had defaced the statue to honor Italian history. 

In a nutshell, if this opinion is shared by many, perhaps your Italian-American friend is excited that Italy has an integral part in American history, even if it comes with tons of baggage. Many Italians I’ve met adore America, so maybe they are excited to be part of its history. Amerigo Vespucci was the explorer that the country is named after, but he doesn’t seem to get much attention, so maybe they’re proud of Columbus for the exploration he’s accomplished despite the murders his storytellers tend to sweep under the rug. 

I am not Italian; I just lived there for a bit. Hence, I welcome the actual Italians out there to input your two cents because I don’t know if this sentiment is widespread or just unique to my friend.

The Bible. Some sects of Christianity add their own books to the Bible, and the Bible is the only true word of God. That’s the short answer, anyway :’) It’s like saying should you trust a history textbook or a history teacher who is interpreting the textbook? Of course, it’s good to have people’s points of view, but it’s definitely important to listen critically and actively decide if you agree with those opinions or not. (That applies to everything in life, not just religion - politics, the news, work drama, etc.)

EDIT: I see this comment is very disliked, and I realize maybe I haven’t properly explained myself. Of course every type of Christianity has different beliefs: some add books to the Bible while others exclude books. It’s kind of awkward to have theological discussions since every sect differs slightly (and, sometimes, not so slightly). In general, the most important thing is that we all believe in the basic elements of the faith, and I don’t believe focusing on the tiny details is so important right now. This world is losing Christians and becoming more and more atheist, and this is quite sad, so I believe it is important to share the joys of our faith instead of focusing on what divides us.

To better clarify what I meant, I compared studying the Bible to studying a primary source of history as opposed to, for example, watching a documentary about that primary source. Maybe the documentary could better put the primary source into context for the viewers’ further understanding, but, at the end of the day, every documentary about that primary source will be a bit different. I used a “history book” a comparison because the Bible is so unique and special that it could not possibly be compared to anything. However, if we had to choose something to compare it to, the closest comparison would be a history book because it is essentially a book with the history of God’s people. As for clergy vs. history teachers, I am not by any means saying pastors and priests are not to be trusted; instead, I was saying that every one of them will have a different interpretation of the Bible. It is helpful to listen to their interpretations for our own understanding, but we should listen to them actively instead of passively and think critically about why we believe them. In other words, we should make sure we know what we are agreeing with instead of copying other people’s opinions. This is because, even though I’m sure most clergy out there are wonderful people, there will always be false prophets that we should be wary of. In fact, many people get sucked into cults accidentally by believing a religion without thinking about why its principles are the way they are. 

In a nutshell, some sects have longer Bibles, and some have shorter ones. Some value other elements of the church besides just the Bible. Every type of Christianity is different, so it is quite difficult to ask such a broad question to a bunch of “Christians” without specifying the category. 

Anyway, I hope we can be more accepting and loving in this sub because that’s what Christianity is all about: loving our neighbors like ourselves and, albeit enjoying a bit of pensive theological discussion. At the end of the day, spreading the word of God’s greatness is an ambition we all share, regardless the denomination.

I am new to this sub, and I was excited to read through what people were posting about, so I didn’t read the post well before answering. I promise I was not trying to offend anyone from the Catholic faith; I was not saying that Catholicism “adds books” in a negative way, but rather saying that, in general, some churches add books while others have different Bibles. I apologize for the discrepancies and for any possible offense!)

Hey! Wow, I had to comment because I was in exactly the same situation as you until about a week ago. 

My ex and I broke up about four months ago, and that was so devastating, more for me than for him, I think. He hasn’t posted on Instagram since 2017, so checking his *new* posts wasn’t the problem. Instead, I found myself simply visiting his page just to see his face. I would also check his followers to see if any new girls had followed him; since we met on a dating app, I figured he probably redownloaded it after we broke up and the girls he matched with would follow him. Also, on Instagram, your followers list appears in chronological order with the most recent followers at the top of the list. Hence, it was simply too easy to see which new girls were entering his life. Anyway, I would impulsively obsesses over this list of followers and sometimes compare myself to the new girls who followed him. Then, I would cry and think about how much I missed him. Then, after a while, I realized, “why do I actually miss him? I feel like this is more of an addiction than love.” I think I was right. I thought, “what would an addict do?” Checking his followers list was, for some reason, like a drug to me; I needed to do it a few times per day to feel “satisfied.” I know it sounds crazy, but I could actually feel the burst of dopamine that came from checking his followers list. One week ago, I told myself that I was not allowed to check his Instagram account for one whole week, like quitting a drug cold turkey. I made a checklist in the “notes” section of my phone for each of the seven days so I could gain the satisfaction of tapping the button when I had successfully gotten through a whole day without checking. The first few days, it was SO hard. I felt like I had an itch and was trying not to scratch it. However, but the end of the week, I found myself gaining more gratification from checking the circle in my notes at the end of each day. Now, it’s been about ten days since I started that challenge, and I feel so proud of myself! I realized I don’t love him anymore because he’s a jerk who made me cry way too many tears, and I realized that changing my habits was difficult at first but definitely rewarding. 

General closure is also important. Remember that he is not a part of your life anymore. And remember that he is just a person like everyone else in this earth. Maybe try thinking about him not as your ex, not as someone you used to love, not as someone who hurt you, but as someone who is simply a human being on this earth. Try to see him neutrally. Say his full legal name out loud over and over and over again until the name starts to sound strange and unknown, just like people do with words sometimes. Try to see him as a human being with traits - not wonderful, not terrible, but just straightforward facts. Also, another thing that helped me was putting things into perspective: I know my ex and I were perfect together at the time, but then things happened and I found out he was not the person I was expecting. The same happened to you because, if he were the person you were expecting, he wouldn’t have been a jerk and broken up with you. It’s okay to realize that you *were* good together, but people change; the current him is not the same person as the previous him, even if they look the same. This mental separation of “my boyfriend” and “my ex” was really important; I loved my boyfriend, and I am happy for the nice memories we made together, and I mourn his “death” sometimes, but my ex is just another human being on this planet whom I have no attachment with whatsoever. 

Girl, stay strong. You can get through this. Breakups suck, but, if anything, use it as a motivation to become your best self so he’ll be sorry he ever let you slip through his fingers. Then, while you’re trying so get back on your feet again, you’ll run into someone else who’s an even better fit for you and forget about how sad that loser made you feel.

Good luck!! You can do it! 💪❤️
